name: Jorim
overview: Jorim is a male figure mentioned in the genealogy of the Messiah as recorded in Luke 3:29. While specific tribal affiliation and additional background details are not provided, his inclusion in this lineage highlights his role in the ancestral line leading to Christ. No further personal notes are recorded about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Jorim means 'y-h-v-h is exalted,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that honors the exaltation of the Lord. This proper name, found in Luke 3:29, is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries significant spiritual weight in its meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Jorim is the son of Eliezer, an inferred relationship, and the father of Matthat, an explicit relationship, both noted in Luke 3:29. These familial connections situate him within the direct ancestral line that leads to the Messiah.
scriptureSignificance: Jorim's significance lies primarily in his place within the Messianic genealogy, marking him as an important link in the lineage culminating in Jesus Christ. His mention in Luke 3:29 underscores the fulfillment of God's promise through a historically grounded ancestry. While the biblical text does not elaborate on his personal deeds, his role affirms the providential unfolding of salvation history through faithful generations.
